subject: She waited a lifetime for this
preview: The Christmas story starts with an old woman and an empty cradle.
linkText: Who Was Elizabeth in the Bible? The Woman Who Waited a Lifetime for a Miracle

blocks.text: Some Bible stories start with a battle. Elizabeth's starts with a wait.
She was married to a good man. She loved God with her whole life.
And year after year, the one thing she wanted most never came.
In her world, a woman without children carried a quiet shame that never really let up.
But Luke goes out of his way to tell us she did nothing wrong.
"And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless."
Two faithful people. No child. Old age arriving with the door still shut.
Then one day an angel stood in the temple and spoke to her husband.
"Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."
Thy prayer is heard.
Not a new prayer. An old one, prayed through all the years when nothing seemed to change.
Here is what I want you to understand.
God's silence is not the same as God's absence.
Elizabeth hid herself for five months, then said the Lord had looked on her "to take away my reproach among men."
In her sixth month, her young relative Mary showed up at the door carrying a secret of her own.
The baby leaped in Elizabeth's womb, and she was filled with the Holy Ghost.
She called Mary "the mother of my Lord" and celebrated Mary's miracle right in the middle of her own.
Her long wait and the birth of Jesus ended up woven into the very same story.
She did not manufacture her miracle. She kept walking with God through years that gave her every reason to give up.
If you are waiting on something this Christmas that feels impossible, her story is for you.
In the full article I walk through Luke 1 in order, all the way to the day she stood against the whole family and said, "Not so; but he shall be called John."
